newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka slaps travel ban on stock scandal accused.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka slaps travel ban on stock scandal accused.

text.p: Bangladesh has banned indefinitely foreign travel by those accused of involvement in the country's stock market scandal, police said on Monday.

A directive from the Home (Interior) Ministry late on Sunday said the list of 36 accused of share price manipulation had been forwarded to immigration officials, including those at Dhaka's Zia International Airport, to prevent them fleeing the country.
"All necessary steps have been taken to ensure they can't slip out while legal action is under way," one police officer said.
Warrants for the arrest of the accused were issued by Dhaka's Chief Metropolitan Magistrate on Wednesday, but 21 of them were later granted bail by the High Court.
The remaining 15 are still in hiding, court officials said.
The arrest warrants were issued after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the capital market watchdog, filed charges against the leading stock market players.

The SEC based its case on a report issued by a committee of inquiry headed by professor Amirul Islam Chowdhury, which said they had been involved in "fraudulent activities", causing unusual fluctuations in share prices and losses to investors.
Chowdhury is vice-chancellor of Jahangirnagar University, near Dhaka.
Those who obtained bail on Sunday included the chairman of Dhaka Stock Exchange, Imtiyaz Husain, and Runa Alam, head of SES Securities Ltd and chief of Peregrine Capital Limited in Bangladesh.
Alam has been charged in connection with her position at SES, but not in relation to her position with Peregrine.
Leading industrialist Salman Rahman and three top executives of his Beximco group of companies were granted bail on Thursday.
